title: A magical night in the Atacama Desert
caption: The Milky Way over Valle de la Luna, Atacama Desert, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Twisted, gnarled rock formations jut from the desert floor like old wizards' hats, while overhead the sky fills with thousands of stars and a wash of colors. This is Valle de la Luna, the "Valley of the Moon", in Chile's Atacama Desert, not far from ALMA, the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, a facility in which ESO is a partner.

The name fits. Aeons of exposure to wind and weather have worn the dried-up salt beds into moon-like shapes that feel more alien than earthly. Above them, the Milky Way pours across the sky, lit by its gas and stars, with vivid red tones that come from hydrogen atoms spread throughout our galaxy.

The valley's altitude, dry air and remoteness also make it a superb spot for stargazing. Dryness matters especially for ALMA, because water vapor in the atmosphere can soak up the invisible light this radio telescope collects.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to P. Horálek/ESO. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The red hydrogen glow and many of the other colors are faint, and a camera gathering light over time may record them far more vividly than the eye.
